250: 4.3. The structure of Deep Interest Network
251: Among all those features of Table 1, user behavior features are critically important and play key roles in modeling user interests in the scenario of e-commerce applications.
252: Base model obtains a fixed-length representation vector of user interests by pooling all the embedding vectors over the user behavior feature group, as Eq.(1). This representation vector stays the same for a given user, in regardless of what candidate ads are.
253: In this way, the user representation vector with a limited dimension will be a bottleneck to express user’s diverse interests.
254: To make it capable enough, an easy method is to expand the dimension of embedding vector, which unfortunately will increase the size of learning parameters heavily.
255: It will lead to overfitting under limited training data and add the burden of computation and storage, which may not be tolerated for an industrial online system.
256: Is there an elegant way to represent user’s diverse interests in one vector under limited dimension?
257: The local activation characteristic of user interests gives us inspiration to design a novel model named deep interest network(DIN).
258: Imagine when the young mother mentioned above in section 3 visits the e-commerce site, she finds the displayed new handbag cute and clicks it.
259: Let’s dissect the driving force of click action.
260: The displayed ad hits the related interests of this young mother by soft-searching her historical behaviors and finding that she had browsed similar goods of tote bag and leather handbag recently.
261: In other words, behaviors related to displayed ad greatly contribute to the click action.
262: DIN simulates this process by paying attention to the representation of locally activated interests w.r.t. given ad.
263: Instead of expressing all user’s diverse interests with the same vector, DIN adaptively calculate the representation vector of user interests by taking into consideration the relevance of historical behaviors w.r.t. candidate ad.
264: This representation vector varies over different ads.
265: The right part of Fig.2 illustrates the architecture of DIN.
